cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a large hand-sewn cotton gown (boubou/tobe) with fine green hand-embroidery, a garment type worn broadly across West African Sahelian groups including the Wolof of Senegal; nothing marks it as belonging to a specific non-Wolof people.

physical.title: gown; tobe
physical.summary: Gown (boubou, tobe, riga): made from 257 strips of hand-spun white cotton hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The tunic area of the gown is flared towards the bottom, and the sleeves are wider at the top than at the bottom. At the front is a vestigial large pocket which has been sewn down. The front and shoulders have been hand-embroidered in European green cotton with a pattern of ‘eight knives’ (aska takwas) and another spiral is on the back. The tunic has been hemmed around the neck, sleeves and base. The bottom of the skirt has been lined with a broad strip of hand-woven cotton composed of alternating diagonal lines in purple, green and indigo thread.
